$comment: Reactor Bots: an in-place upgrade of the ordinary Iron Teeth bot (user direction 2026-10-29: same bot, same template, saved per-bot flag). Written by tools/super_bot_content.mjs; runtime src/DeepFrontier/Scripts/SuperBots; checked by tools/validate_super_bots.mjs. Every value is authored here; the generator and the runtime have no defaults.

upgrade.$comment: Per-bot buffs. carryingCapacityBonus is a native BonusManager delta (CarryingCapacity, clamped 0.1..10): +4 gives x5. Speed cannot use the native MovementSpeed bonus (clamped at 2.0), so ReactorBotPatches multiplies WalkerSpeedManager's base speed. workingSpeedMultiplier (user 2026-11-02: "500% working speed base") is the native WorkingSpeed bonus (clamped 0.05..1000) that Worker.WorkingSpeedMultiplier reads for production, construction, planting, yield removal, demolition and the work animations: a delta of workingSpeedMultiplier - 1 takes the base from 1 to 5; wellbeing tiers add their native deltas on top. lifespanMultiplier divides all wear (native, workplace and unplated). unplatedWearMultiplier applies while the plating need is not favourable. A bot finished by the Bot Assembler's Reactor bot recipe (id IndustrialBot) is born with this upgrade (tools/workforce_risks.json botAssembly). Skin (user 2026-11-02: after build 252 "radioactive yellow eyes" and "dark tones"; after the first renders "neon yellow, bright yellow" glowing eyes and glow "in between the joints", "like a glow"; the game's shader stays): the bot body's BotURP shader (official BotURP.shadergraph) has no _LightingColor, its eye cyan is painted in _BaseMap and baked into the _BaseMap_1 emission map (x2 with bloom), and a CharacterTint multiplies the whole body and adds 0.35 x tint as glow, so the skin is a texture set made at runtime from the bot's own maps and body mesh (src/DeepFrontier/Scripts/SuperBots/ReactorBotSkin.cs), set through native CharacterMaterialModifier.SetTexture. glow.color is a neon yellow of the radiation hue (RadiationMaterials.WaterTintColor, hue checked by tools/validate_super_bots.mjs) at full saturation and value; it is painted on the eyes and joint seams and, times glow.intensity (linear), written to an HDR emission map, so they glow by day and bloom at night. Joint seams: near each glow.joints pivot (bind-pose model space of the bot body mesh, measured; mirrorX adds the left side), the surface within glow.rim of another mesh part, x glow.jointGain. darkPlating (c/255)^gamma x scale x color darkens the body while the plating need is favourable (the vanilla light body, still glowing, while unplated). illumination is the native bot illumination colour (MaterialColorer, as vanilla BotIlluminationController sets IlluminationColor.Bot 0.16/0.59/0.80), the glow colour; the BotURP body does not read it.

leak.$comment: User 2026-11-02: "If they overheat or go unmaintained for too long then they can leak radioactive water on the ground." A Reactor Bot whose coolant need (needs.coolant) has been in its native critical state (overheating) for more than overheatHours, or whose plating need (needs.plating) has been exhausted for more than unmaintainedHours, leaks volumePerHour radioactive water (native water units; one RadioactiveSludge good is 0.2) through IRadiationService.AddRadioactiveWater: one pulse at once, then one every pulseHours, until both are fixed. Lifespan wear is not a condition (every bot ages however well it is kept). Where: the bot's cell, or the doorstep of the building it is inside, then the radiation system's TryFindOpenCell. For scale, a full Radioactive Waste Vault or a blocked Waste Refinery leaks 1.2 per day (0.05 per hour). Runtime src/DeepFrontier/Scripts/SuperBots/ReactorBotLeak.cs.

$consumption: Bot-only ConsumptionEffects added to these goods: bots take one unit from storage as beavers eat (native InventoryNeedBehavior). Beavers never take them (the needs are not theirs); ordinary bots have them disabled.
$parts: A queued bot is retrofitted by taking one Reinforced Bot Frame and one Reactor Power Cell from storage (each fills its retrofit need); the upgrade applies when every retrofit need is full. Second use of both parts: the Reactor Charging Bay construction gate (tools/building_construction_costs.json lategameGates). Third: the Bot Assembler's Reactor bot recipe (id IndustrialBot), which builds a Reactor Bot from both parts, four limbs and a head (tools/workforce_risks.json botAssembly).

station.$comment: Native powered goods-consuming attraction (vanilla DecontaminationPod / MudBath contract) on the vanilla ChargingStation.IronTeeth template. It serves only ReactorCharge, so ordinary bots never use it, and Reactor Bots never use the vanilla station (Energy is disabled on them). Geometry, model and slots: tools/asset-pipeline/lategame_ReactorChargingBay.py. Menu (user 2026-11-02): right after the vanilla Charging Station in Science (ChargingStation ToolOrder 70, ControlTower 80), declared as an upgrade in tools/tool_groups.json upgrades. Science 300,000 since 2026-11-03 (was 400,000; docs/deadlock-audit.md D6, user approved P2): with the Uranium Processing Plant, which makes the reactor power cells that Reactor Bots (recipe and retrofit) and the bay itself need, so no Reactor Bot exists before a place to charge it.
